features.gap: BEGIN is sent immediately on every transaction block, even ones that run no query or only reads that a cache satisfies; AR defers BEGIN until the first statement. Deferred: Low value, effort L, and lazy checkout mid-block risks starving the pool. Revisit after T01 lands and benchmarks show empty-transaction cost.

features.feature: Current transaction object and per-transaction callbacks (Rails 7.2)
Row-lock unsaved-changes guard (lock! / with_lock on a dirty record)
Relation#lock with a custom SQL clause or false
Constraint-violation exception mapping (RecordNotUnique, InvalidForeignKey, NotNullViolation, ValueTooLong)
Statement failure wrapper carrying sql and binds (StatementInvalid)
features.gap: None for sqlite and pg. The builder, executors, aggregations, querying.cr, connection.cr and the connection facade carry sql (proven path by path); any other bare Adapter#open now falls back to the statement last built on the failing connection (DB::Connection#grant_last_sql), so migration and seed helpers also name it. Binds stay redacted unless capture_statement_bind_values, and are capped.

features.feature: Lock/timeout exception translation (Deadlocked, LockWaitTimeout, StatementTimeout, QueryCanceled, SerializationFailure)
Connection/pool error types (ConnectionTimeoutError, ConnectionNotEstablished, ConnectionFailed, NoDatabaseError)
features.gap: None for sqlite and pg. A live connect to a missing PostgreSQL database (cause PQError 3D000) or a SQLite file in a missing directory raises NoDatabaseError; a refused port raises ConnectionFailed with the DB::ConnectionRefused cause; a held pool raises ConnectionTimeoutError live. MySQL errno 1049 is classified by the existing translator but was not run live.

features.feature: Pool disconnect and teardown (disconnect!, clear_all_connections!, remove_connection)
Checked-out connection block (with_connection / lease_connection / permanent lease)
features.gap: The permanent lease (lease_connection) is deliberately designed out because pinning a connection for a whole request starves the pool; with_connection is block-scoped, released in ensure, and joins transactions and nested calls, proven on sqlite and pg. Nothing else is open.

Database URL / DATABASE_URL configuration and adapter inference from URL scheme
Database configurations API (db_config, configs_for, per-environment named configs)

features.gap: None for sqlite and pg. Same as the Multiple databases row: every explicit shard swap is guarded; data-driven routing is deliberately not a swap.

features.gap: There is no per-connection variables hook, so statement_timeout, lock_timeout, application_name, default search_path and MySQL sql_mode cannot be set declaratively; no per-query timeout. MySQL adapter only forces utf8mb4 encoding. Deferred: crystal-db has no on-connect hook, so this needs an upstream or wrapped-connection factory. A SET on every checkout would double round trips.

features.feature: Literal question-mark escaping in raw SQL fragments

features.gap: none. merge appends the other relation's ORDER BY (a reorder on the other side replaces), applies the other relation's unscoping, and the named-scope path (merge_builder) now replaces same-column equality and appends order. from and CTE merge already existed and are now specced.

none. Added :from/:with/:readonly/:optimizer_hints (specced), :annotate, :create_with, :reordering, :left_joins, :strict_loading and :extending. :extending is a deliberate no-op because a Grant relation holds no per-relation extension modules (extending is a compile-time model macro). Default-scope clauses and raw SQL string conditions stay on purpose (tenant/soft-delete isolation; ActiveRecord also does not remove raw strings by column).

features.feature: extending (adding methods to a relation at runtime)
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby extends relation instances with arbitrary modules at runtime; Crystal uses static types and compile-time extensions.

features.gap: none. reorder(String | Grant.sql | field, direction, nulls:), reselect and regroup with String, Symbol, mixed and Array forms.

none open. Association scopes are rendered once in the ON clause (inlined as escaped literals; no extra query); a table reached twice (joins(:comments, posts: :comments), self-referential associations) is aliased automatically (comments_posts style); raw fragments take ? binds; through paths of any depth and scopes on each hop join. Polymorphic belongs_to joins raise ArgumentError, which matches ActiveRecord. Arel/block join nodes are not applicable in Crystal (no Arel); raw SQL with binds and typed association joins cover the use.

none. Scoped associations (including a scope on a through association and on the association it goes through), has_one, composite-key associations, nested through, and through a polymorphic has_many as: source or a polymorphic source with source_type: all work through EXISTS / NOT EXISTS with bound scope values. A polymorphic belongs_to still raises, as in ActiveRecord.

features.gap: none open. Added update(hash), update(id, hash), update(ids, attributes_list) (each id gets its own attributes, one SELECT then per-record update, scoped to the relation, also Model.update/update!), update(:all, ...) and update! twins. Deliberate difference kept: update! rolls back only the batch of 1000 in progress (one transaction per batch for speed); ActiveRecord leaves earlier records saved. Wrap the call in Model.transaction for all-or-nothing, which is specced.

features.feature: many? / one? / none? / empty? efficient existence-count predicates

features.gap: none open. :includes, :preload, :eager_load (also takes back the joins and DISTINCT eager_load added), :strict_loading, :readonly, :optimizer_hints, :annotate, :create_with, :reordering, :left_joins, :extending are recognized. Default-scope clauses are intentionally left in place (tenant/soft-delete safety); unscoped is the explicit way to drop them.
none. Same implementation as where.missing; polymorphic belongs_to raises as in ActiveRecord.

where.not with hash / multi-condition (NAND) and non-scalar values
or / and with a relation argument and structural-compatibility check

features.gap: none open. Model.new, create, create!, build inside a scoping block start from the relation's equality predicates and create_with defaults (explicit args win; row hydration is not seeded); a parent class's scoping relation reaches STI subclasses (merged over the subclass's own default scope and type filter, hidden by unscoped). Fibers spawned inside the block do not inherit it, same as ActiveRecord's isolated execution state. default_scope attributes are still not applied to Model.new outside a scoping block (not part of this row).

features.not_applicable_reason: references exists so includes can guess JOIN vs preload by parsing string conditions at runtime; Grant selects the strategy explicitly (includes/preload/eager_load).

features.gap: The MySQL below 8 raise is proven only offline (the spec pins a 5.7 adapter and calls ensure_supported!), with no live MySQL server. The recursive depth guard requires the step to be SELECT ... FROM ... [WHERE ...]. A raw recursive body needs unguarded: true. update_all and delete_all emit no WITH.

WhereChain offers string-field predicates (where.gt(:age, 18)) but no typed column objects that compose (Post.arel_table[:id].gt(1).and(...)), no OR-ing of predicates, no reuse across where/order/select/having/joins conditions. Deferred: Effort L. Its value depends on stable relation immutability (Q01) and where composition (Q02). Consider a typed-column design in a later release, not this program.
Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

Single hop only, and the source must be a belongs_to. Nested (multi-hop) through, source_type:, a has_many source (raises ThroughWriteError), disable_joins, and cross-database loading are still missing. Appending a target that is already linked, while the collection is not loaded, inserts a duplicate join row (ActiveRecord behaves the same, with no unique index).

Everything in the implementer's list. In addition, the check for whether through: names an association runs at macro time against methods already defined on this class only. If the through association is declared later, or on a parent class, the code silently falls back to the legacy table-name reader: an N+1 on preload, and bad SQL if no table has that name.
The create_join_table migration helper is missing (the spec creates the join table by hand). Join columns are Int64 only. There is no scope argument and no extend option.

Done and spec'd: UUID/String keys via typed foreign_key declaration, preload of has_many/has_one as:, has_one as: setter and caching, polymorphic_name (STI root), registration, has_many as: returns AssociationCollection with the type predicate in SQL, dependent delete_all/delete/nullify/destroy. Not covered: dependent :restrict and :restrict_with_exception on the as: side are implemented but have no spec; an STI subclass (not the root) that declares has_many as: registers under its own name so a stored root name will not resolve through load_polymorphic; a String foreign key over UUID has_many owners is not supported (only belongs_to normalizes keys to text).

The switch from includes to a JOIN only happens on the load path (select/first/each). count, exists? and pluck on an includes relation whose where names the association table still do not join; a probe confirmed count raises ArgumentError 'Unknown query field "ni_cities.name"', where AR counts over the join. When the where contains an OR, the association now loads all its rows (a superset) because a flat WHERE cannot be replayed; AR would hold only the joined rows. An association scope that uses .or still renders flat on the preload query (a OR b AND fk IN (...)), which over-fetches rows; that is a builder precedence issue owned by Q01. eager_load of a polymorphic belongs_to raises stdlib ArgumentError, not a Grant::ErrorBase error.

Done: association strict_loading: true/false option, Model.strict_loading_by_default, strict_loading!(value, mode), :n_plus_one_only, propagation to loaded records (lazy and preloaded), Grant.settings.strict_loading_violation = :raise | :log, polymorphic has_many/has_one/belongs_to readers assert; spec has no responds_to? guards. Gap: strict_loading_by_default is keyed by class name and not inherited by subclasses (set it on each model, or on Grant::Base for a global default); Relation#strict_loading has no mode argument (builder.cr strict_loading region belongs to Q01).

None. The implementer's report said non-Int64 keys were not exercised. I added a String-key spec (typed foreign_key: String?, String primary key, reader, id reader, includes preload, dependent: :destroy). It passes on both adapters. UUID keys are not exercised. Notes: build_entryable takes the class plus named attributes. dependent: supports :destroy and :delete only and is not wrapped in an extra transaction.

Scope now applies in SQL on preload, lazy readers, and for belongs_to and has_one (zero-arg expression form and ->(q : Builder(T)) form). Still missing: extend: module/block extensions, instance-dependent scopes ->(q, owner), scope on polymorphic as: associations, scope honored by dependent:.

none. _ids and _ids= are generated for plain, through: and as: has_many. The reader is typed to the key column (Array(Int64)), numeric strings are cast to the key type, and the writer saves each added record (validations, callbacks, updated_at touch run) while removals stay set-based. For as: collections an unsaved owner raises OwnerNotSaved because polymorphic has_many has no autosave.

none. Built records now show up in reads (to_a, each, size, any?, empty?, first, last, find_by) of an unloaded collection, plain and through, on saved and unsaved owners. Array create deliberately stays one transaction with one INSERT per record: ActiveRecord's create([..]) does the same (create is not insert_all), so a multi-row insert would skip validations and callbacks.

features.feature: belongs_to validates the referenced record, not only foreign-key presence
singular association builders build_<assoc> / create_<assoc> / create_<assoc>!
features.gap: none for belongs_to and has_one. Like ActiveRecord, not generated for polymorphic belongs_to, has_one :as, or has_one :through. Takes **attributes only (no positional hash, no block).

features.feature: stale-target detection when a belongs_to/has_one foreign key changes
features.gap: After `item.owner = a; item.owner_id = b.id` the reader still returns a (probe P8). AR compares the cached target's key to the current FK and reloads.

features.feature: has_one / has_many writer persists and replaces on assignment
features.gap: none for has_one, has_many, has_many through, has_one as: and has_many as:. On a saved owner the writer runs in one transaction: removed records follow dependent (nullify/delete/destroy, set-based), new ones are saved, RecordNotSaved/RecordInvalid rolls everything back. AssociationCollection#replace and #concat exist. Unsaved owners keep the staging behavior. Mass assignment (set_attributes, nested attributes, composite associations) deliberately keeps the in-memory staging path.

features.feature: association collection as a chainable relation (order/limit/pluck/sum/distinct/select/find_each)
features.gap: none. AssociationCollection#scope is public; explicit delegators cover order, offset, limit, lock, joins, left_joins, distinct, having, none, reorder, reverse_order, rewhere, reselect, regroup, group, pluck, pick, pluck_as, pick_as, includes, preload, eager_load, find_each, find_in_batches, in_batches, average, minimum, maximum, calculate, sum, select(*cols), unscope, explain, plus all where forms. Each runs as SQL (one statement asserted) and does not load the association; Enumerable stays the in-memory path for loaded records. Works for scoped and through collections.

features.feature: collection ordinal finders and multi-id find (first(n), last(n), take, second..fifth, find(*ids))
features.gap: none. first/last/take (plus bang forms), first(n), last(n), take(n), second..fifth, forty_two, second_to_last, third_to_last, find(ids), find(a, b, *rest), find!(ids) use LIMIT/OFFSET/ORDER BY pk or one IN query and never hydrate the association; loaded or unsaved-holding collections answer from memory. find with a block remains Enumerable#find.

none. All three (plus ! forms, block and Hash forms) are on the collection and go through build/create so the owner key, inverse, hooks and the through join row are applied. create_or_find_by inserts inside a savepoint, issues no prior SELECT, and falls back to find_by on RecordNotUnique (verified with a unique index on both adapters).

features.feature: has_many :through collection writers (<<, build, create, delete, clear, <assoc>_ids=)
features.gap: none. <<, concat, build, create, create!, delete(record...), clear, <assoc>_ids= and the new <assoc>= writer all work on through collections: targets saved first, one multi-row join INSERT and one DELETE ... IN, all in a transaction, rolled back when a target is invalid, deferred to owner save for unsaved owners.

none for reads: lazy reader, count, exists?, where, find, ids, raw all(clause), and includes preload all work for chains of any depth, including a source that is itself a through. Nested through is read-only, as in ActiveRecord (writes raise ThroughWriteError). Not covered: a scope lambda on an association whose source is itself a through raises ThroughChainError on preload; intermediate models' default scopes are not applied to the join hops; has_one through a nested through was not specced separately.

none. source_type: Post on has_many/has_one :through, read with one statement (type predicate in the join), preload with one query per hop, scope lambda supported, << and delete write the type, and a polymorphic source without source_type raises ThroughChainError. The through-writer for a polymorphic source was not specced for destroy/delete_all beyond delete(record).

No option; Grant's through query already uses an IN subquery rather than a JOIN, so cross-database through is not available. Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

features.feature: validate: option and validation of new associated records on owner save
dependent honors the association scope and has_many :through join rows
features.gap: none for the stated gap. Scoped has_many and has_one now act only on the scoped relation for destroy, delete_all, nullify, restrict_with_error and restrict_with_exception, via a new Grant::Associations._grant_scoped_dependent macro used only when a scope is given (unscoped models generate nothing new). The through join-row behavior was verified and already correct (setup_dependent_through). The scoped destroy_async path is implemented the same way but has no spec (it needs the async enqueuer).

features.gap: none. Unknown keys fail at macro expansion for belongs_to, has_one, has_many (including as:/polymorphic paths, typed declarations, habtm's forwarded options); source_type without through fails; dependent: values were already checked by Grant::Dependent.check_dependent_option and are covered per type here. The direct belongs_to_polymorphic / has_many_polymorphic macros are not separately validated.

through, as, polymorphic, counter_cache, touch and autosave are compile errors; no required-parent validation; where.associated/missing and where(assoc: record) are not adapted for composite associations. MySQL not run.

Grant::Preloader.new(records, [:posts, {comments: [:author]}]).call (also splat and keyword forms) with recursive Includes, AssociationNotFoundError, skip of already-loaded associations, IN chunking, one query per level. Missing: the optional scope proc argument.
